title: Network People Services Technologies Ltd - 544396 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 2.4x YoY to INR 68.46 crore; FY26 revenue about INR 209 crore with EBITDA near INR 65 crore, with management guiding ~70% CAGR to INR 850-900 crore by FY29.
summary.overview: Management framed FY26 as a transformation year, shifting mix away from PPaaS toward TSP, with international, SaaS and RegTech as the planned growth drivers. Q4 revenue was about INR 68.46 crore, EBITDA INR 19.26 crore and net profit INR 12.24 crore, and the call noted Q4 as the lowest EBITDA margin quarter. FY26 operating cash flow was negative, which management attributed to longer TSP credit periods. Management guided to ~70% revenue CAGR over three years, with the first-year (FY27) run-rate on the order of INR 340-350 crore, and said the mix shift would lift margins over time.

financial_highlights.change: full-year EBITDA margin cited at 31% vs 37% prior year (analyst figure)
net profit fell 9.7% per analyst question; PAT margin about 20% vs 25%
reason: longer credit period in TSP business

financial_highlights.value: about 180 days expected going forward (analyst interpretation, not confirmed by management)
financial_highlights.change: expected to decline gradually as mix changes

segments.name: TSP (Technology Service Provider)
segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 90% of FY26 business per management; slide 17 shows TSP tapering to 30-40% of business contribution by FY29, with absolute value expected to rise. Carries longer credit periods and low-to-medium margins.

segments.name: PPaaS (Payment Platform as a Service)
segments.commentary: Management said more than a year of effort has not delivered desired results; engine being pivoted to domestic merchant orchestration and global PPaaS. Guided at 5-8% contribution in FY27-FY29 per analyst reading of slides; about 40+ accounts in funnel.

segments.name: RegTech
segments.commentary: AI-led RegTech product bought by one large public sector bank; close talks with multiple public and private banks. Purely SaaS; management expects revenue contribution from FY27 and guided 10-15% contribution range per analyst reading.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Zero base in FY26; guided to about 25% of business in FY27, 40% in FY28 and about 50% in FY29 per analyst reading. Management said about 40% of FY27 international business is already in hand, and bagged a large RegTech order including a central payment body abroad. Mix of license and SaaS.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of about 70% over three years; FY29 revenue INR 850-900 crore per management (analyst cited ~INR 950 crore), from FY26 base of about INR 209 crore.
FY27 growth of about 70% targeted; analyst-proposed FY27 range INR 340-350 crore accepted as 'anything around that range'.

EBITDA margin expected to rise over time to a range of roughly 40-50% at the end of the period, with the timing tied to Slide 17 blocks; management said FY26 margin pressure would reverse in FY27 and FY28, and that PAT margin returns to 25% by this financial year.
Operating cash flow conversion expected to improve as TSP credit periods shorten; no specific conversion figure given.
AI targets: 30% efficiency in support functions, 50% faster development, 1.5x capacity from existing business; RegTech AI revenue from FY27; revenue per employee up 300% in three years.
Market growth cited: payment processing 22% CAGR, RegTech ~32%, digital lending and orchestration above 40%.
capex_capacity: Investment in SaaS-based hosted engine targeted to reach at least 200 tenants in TSP verticals by FY29.
Pipeline of about 40+ PPaaS accounts and about 10 countries under international evaluation.
About 9 accounts added in Bank-in-a-Box and payment devices in Q4; about 2 PAC orders received recently; entered IoT-based payment solution with a new fintech.
Project expenses reportedly up about 60% in the presentation, attributed to new product line capacity and the PPaaS-to-TSP shift; management said new development is not charged to P&L.

Unallocated Tata Mutual Fund funds (INR 300 crore referenced by analyst): management said no inorganic deal has been signed; some deals rejected after due diligence; deployment expected in global assets and beyond-payments areas (RegTech, lending).
demand_pricing: Management said 8 of 10 RegTech pitches go into POC or sales pitch; described demand as a pseudo-mandate from bank CRO and CISO functions.
Competition in AI RegTech described as limited for now; management expects competition in about two years, citing three years of build effort.

International pricing: management said margins could run 25-50% higher than India-level margins, with some engagements at 50-60% higher; the company declined some licence deals with unfavourable payment terms.
Large OPEX deal signed in which revenue is triggered on each milestone; management expects lumpy quarters before a steadier base from FY28-FY29.
Management said credit period reflects TSP mix and will reduce with mix shift; analyst-cited receivable days of about 180 are not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 operating cash flow negative and what EBITDA-to-OCF conversion is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Aggarwal attributed it to the shift from PPaaS to TSP, which carries longer credit periods; expects conversion to improve gradually as international and other mix rises. No numeric conversion target given.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is the 70% CAGR and when will EBITDA reach 33-35%?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Thakur said confidence is high given the funnel: about 200 SaaS tenants, about 10 international countries, and 40+ PPaaS accounts. Said full-year FY26 margin impact came from TSP mix, and balancing the year should bring EBITDA back to prior levels; no quarter given for 33-35%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the absolute revenue numbers for FY27-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 850-900 crore by end FY29 off the INR 209 crore FY26 base; the 70% CAGR is not uniform, with heavier triggers from large projects; FY27 about 70% growth targeted.

qa_highlights.question: How much of FY27 international revenue is already secured?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40% is in hand at the start of the year, with the balance dependent on advanced discussions expected to convert in Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management defined high margin as above 70% over India margin, with international margins of 30-40% or more on a 15-20% India base; the gap is due to the product being roughly 5-6 years ahead of the target markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for PPaaS given weak results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pivoting PPaaS to merchant orchestration domestically and to global markets; two advanced discussions expected to close by end Q1 or early Q2; will not over-invest until results show.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profitability decline and what is the status of the Tata Mutual Fund funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin decline attributed to the mix shift from high-margin PPaaS to low-margin TSP. Some inorganic deals were rejected after due diligence; the company is looking for a deal that gives instant global presence and execution, or moves into RegTech and lending; no deployment made yet.

risks_watch: Negative FY26 operating cash flow and high TSP receivable days; watch for FY27 cash conversion and receivable day reduction.
FY27 revenue heavily dependent on international and large OPEX deal triggers, with about 60% of international FY27 business not yet secured.
Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin the lowest in the year; full-year margin fell to about 31% vs 37% prior; PAT margin down from 25% to about 20%.
PPaaS revival has not delivered; management has not committed to a revised number for the segment.
Use of Tata Mutual Fund proceeds unclear; no inorganic deal announced.
Management's comment on FY26 TSP share (about 90%) and the slide-17 contribution figures were not fully reconciled to absolute values; absolute revenue for each vertical not disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth targets and the RegTech/AI and international pipeline, but noticeably less precise on margins, cash flow and deal timing, often answering with qualitative framing rather than figures. Admitted PPaaS efforts have underdelivered.
key_quotes: I would call FY26 a year of transformation, de-risking, and rebuilding NPST for sustainable, scalable, and diversified growth.
The confidence on 70% CAGR for three years is high because we have a very, very strong funnel.
We are in the range of INR 850 crores to INR 900 crores by the end of FY29.
Almost 40% is in our kitty right now at the beginning of the year.

growth.why: Management guides ~70% revenue CAGR to INR 850-900 crore by FY29 (FY27 run-rate ~INR 340-350 crore) and a margin turnaround to 40-50% EBITDA; backing is partial, resting on international (about 40% of FY27 international business in hand), a RegTech order and a pipeline of about 40+ PPaaS accounts, with no specific capacity additions or utilisation given.
